implementation_notes: serde has no field-selection concept, so the projection lives at the boundary: derive Serialize for the complete resource, turn it into a serde_json::Value, validate the requested names against the allowlist, and retain only those keys (Map::retain) before writing the reply. For hot paths a wrapper type whose Serialize implementation consults the mask avoids building the discarded values, but the Value form is the idiomatic starting point.
pitfalls: serde_json::to_value materializes the whole document (including #[serde(flatten)]/untagged payloads), so the projection saves bytes but not CPU.
Map::retain only exists for objects: a newtype or tuple struct serializes to a non-object, and unchecked unwrapping turns a shape change into a panic.
Unbounded caller input: cap the number of requested paths and prefer a BTreeSet for stable ordering (HashSet iteration order destabilizes ETag/hash comparisons).
Borrowed fields in the source struct become owned clones as soon as they pass through Value - an allocation per selected field.

variants.name: prost_types::FieldMask trim in a tonic service
variants.idiom_name: read_mask: FieldMask validated against the descriptor and applied via a trim loop
variants.implementation_notes: tonic/prost services take the mask as prost_types::FieldMask (usually a read_mask field or a gRPC metadata system parameter). prost gives the mask type but no FieldMaskUtil, so the trim loop is explicit: iterate the paths, copy the covered fields into a fresh message and reject anything the descriptor does not contain. The descriptor, not a hand-written list, is the field vocabulary - which keeps validation exact.
pitfalls: Proto3 scalar defaults make a trimmed field indistinguishable from an unset one unless the message uses optional fields or wrappers - clients cannot tell 'not requested' from 'empty'.
An empty paths vector means 'all fields' in protobuf semantics; treating it as 'no fields' silently empties every reply after an unrelated change.
JSON (lowerCamelCase) and proto (snake_case) path spellings must be converted in one place, or valid requests start failing validation.
